title: On Greeting the guests at the gate
subtitle: 旅行见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：greet　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 greet 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the fisherman ① greeted the guests at the gate in public, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② greets the guests at the gate in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ greet the guests at the gate at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ greeted the guests at the gate before — a line in the logbook for July 1963 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Greeting the guests at the gate in public, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ greet the travellers at the bend in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Greet the travellers at the bend at once and never mention it again.

By 1976 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ greets the travellers at the bend in public every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ greeted the guests at the gate again when nobody else would.

⑩ To greet the guests at the gate, my mother said in 1981, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody greets the guests at the gate in silence again and somebody must greet the guests at the gate in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 迎接（一般过去式 greeted the guests at the gate：1969 年渔人头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 迎接（一般现在 greets the guests at the gate：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 迎接（不定式 to greet the guests at the gate：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 迎接（过去完成时 had greeted the guests at the gate：1963 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 迎接（动名词 greeting the guests at the gate 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 映入（greet the travellers at the bend：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去映入在河湾处迎面撞见旅人）
G. v. 映入（greet the travellers at the bend：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 迎接（后段两处：新来的船工照例 greets the travellers at the bend，而母亲又一次 greeted the guests at the gate）

answers.why: greet 意为“迎接”，1969 年渔人当着众人面迎接在门口迎候客人，那是渔港里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 greeted。
greet 意为“迎接”，自那以后渔人一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 greets。
greet 意为“迎接”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯迎接在门口迎候客人”，此处为不定式 to greet the guests at the gate。
greet 意为“迎接”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 1976 年之前就有人迎接过，故用过去完成时 had greeted。
greet 意为“迎接”，渔人说“迎接在门口迎候客人这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 greeting the guests at the gate 作主语。
greet 意为“映入”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去映入在河湾处迎面撞见旅人”，should ever 之后用原形 greet the travellers at the bend。
greet 意为“映入”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻映入在河湾处迎面撞见旅人（greet the travellers at the bend at once），以后再也不要提起。
greet 意为“迎接”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例映入在河湾处迎面撞见旅人，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 greets。
greet 意为“迎接”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面迎接在门口迎候客人，用一般过去式 greeted 叙述。
greet 意为“迎接”，结尾那句是母亲 1981 年的话：要迎接在门口迎候客人，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 greet 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1969 the fisherman greeted the guests at the gate in public, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman greets the guests at the gate in silence whenever the harbour asks.
Greeting the guests at the gate in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever greet the travellers at the bend in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour greets the travellers at the bend in public every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother greeted the guests at the gate again, and the harbour remembered that half.
